messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: REAL-TIME: p99 latency detector triggered for route=/v1/generate region=us-east-1 current_p99=1.25s threshold=1.0s. Auto-page oncall (sev=P1). Link: https://redwood/alerts/p99-detector

pagerduty: Paging maya chen (primary oncall). Please acknowledge.

maya chen: acknowledged, jumping in. Any immediate errors showing up in logs?

rob patel: seeing a rapid p99 climb tied to streaming sessions. Traces show frequent grpc 'deadline exceeded' on downstream model servers and many stalled Read loops. Quick query: `sum(rate(stream_stalls_total{region="us-east-1"}[2m])) by (host)` -> spike across multiple hosts. p95 around 0.7s, p99 ~1.25s.

anika singh: checking caching layer metrics. prefix_cache_miss_rate for model-gpt-xl jumped at 3412345820; cache eviction_rate spiked. Also rolling restart of cache-agent job happened ~3412345800 as part of a config change.

leo ramirez: that restart was part of a phased rollout for cache-agent v3.2. We flagged a template tweak earlier but assumed it to be safe. I'm digging into the rollout logs now.

maya chen: OK immediate triage: 1) if streaming stalls are causing client-side stalls, enable streaming degradation policy to send short responses (fallback) for active sessions as emergency mitigation; 2) scale model workers in us-east-1 +15 nodes; 3) pause the cache-agent rollout and revert config if necessary. rob -> scale, leo -> pause rollout, anika -> verify cache config & surface bad hosts.

rob patel: scaling now: `POST /ops/pools/scale?pool=inference-us-east-1&add=15`. Console: https://console.redwood/ops/pools/inference-us-east-1. Autoscaler acknowledged, starting new nodes (ETA 3-5m).

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook invoked: streaming-degrade-fallback. Activated by maya chen. This will force-stream-fallback for sessions where kv cache miss > 0.5.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused: cache-agent v3.2 rollout paused at 3/10 hosts due to health anomalies. See https://deploys.redwood/rollouts/cache-agent/v3.2

anika singh: confirmed: config change accidentally set `max_prefix_keys=1` which caused aggressive eviction under load. Patch rolling now to restore `max_prefix_keys=10000` and restart the local agent. Patch pushed to 3 hosts immediately.

leo ramirez: preparing rollback PR as safety. Holding further rollout until postmortem checks.

maya chen: timeline notes: alert at 3412345899, config change around 3412345800, rollout paused at 3412345905. If we don't see p99 drop in 4m, we'll start targeted traffic steering to other regions for critical enterprise routes.

rob patel: 3m update: 9/15 new model nodes healthy. p99 trending down from 1.25s -> 0.88s for us-east-1. Streaming stalls metric decreased ~70%. No elevated 5xx from model tier.

anika singh: patched remaining hosts; prefix hit_rate back up: 0.79 overall. Host-level telemetry shows patched hosts recovered faster.

rob patel: p99 now 0.82s, p95 0.45s in 5m window. Running additional checks on long-tail traces to ensure no silent retries.

maya chen: marking incident as mitigated for active paging. Customer impact: several customers saw degraded tail latency and increased client-side retries for ~10-20 minutes. No data loss. Action items: 1) security/infra to revert bad template change in infra repo (leo), 2) add rollout pipeline assertions to prevent extreme cache config values (leo/anika), 3) add an alert for sudden prefix_hit_rate drops (rob).

leo ramirez: opening PR to update infra templates and adding a unit test to catch `max_prefix_keys` < 10.

anika singh: I'll add the prometheus alert: `prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.5 for 2m` for critical models and update runbook steps for cache-agent rollbacks.

maya chen: scheduling a 45-min postmortem tomorrow to capture detection, mitigations, and next steps. I'll notify CSMs for impacted enterprise accounts. Thanks all for rapid response. Please add any follow-up notes here.

rob patel: follow-up suggestion: implement a short-circuit fallback to medium model for streaming routes when p99 > 1.0s for >90s. I'll draft a proposal.

anika singh: noted to correlate cache-agent rollouts with canary traffic that exercises streaming paths.

maya chen: closing active page; monitors still watchful. If any regression ping `@maya chen`. :white_check_mark:
